title: 9.10 A 93%-Peak-Efficiency Battery-Input 12-to-36V-Output Inductor-in-the-Middle Hybrid Boost Converter with Continuous Input and Output Currents and Fast Transient with No RHP Zero
problem: Conventional boost converters face challenges in high voltage conversion ratios with very short turn-on pulses, significant voltage stress on inductors and transistors, and inherent right-half-plane zero that limits transient response speed.
motivation: Emerging applications like LiDAR transceivers for autonomous driving and motor drivers for robotics/drones require higher voltages and faster transient responses than conventional converters can provide.
method: Proposes a hybrid inductor-in-the-middle topology that reduces voltage stress on components, mitigates the RHP zero issue, and enables faster transient response while maintaining continuous input and output currents for improved efficiency and reliability.
key_novelty: Inductor-in-the-middle architecture eliminating the RHP zero limitation and reducing voltage stress across power switches in high-ratio boost conversion.
contributions: Fast transient response without right-half-plane zero constraint
Continuous input and output currents reducing EMI and stress
Improved reliability and power density for LiDAR and motor applications
primary_theme: High-efficiency hybrid boost converter for emerging edge applications
